newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ENGLAND CAPTAIN ATHERTON FAILS AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND CAPTAIN ATHERTON FAILS AGAIN.

text.p: England took command of their four-day match against Northern Districts on Saturday although captain Mike Atherton remained out of the runs.

After dismissing Northern Districts for just 69, England reached 166 for four by the close of the first day. But it was Atherton's batting problems which continued to plague England's lead-up to the first test against New Zealand, starting in Auckland next Friday.
He made just five in 19 balls before being trapped leg before by young medium pacer Scott Styris.
Atherton's two innings in New Zealand so far have produced 12 runs, and on his tour of Zimbabwe and New Zealand he has scored only 208 in 15 innings.
England's bowlers looked ominous as they ripped through Northern Districts.
Dominic Cork removed New Zealand's test openers Blair Pocock and Bryan Young in his first 16 balls of the day for nought and four respectively, and Northern Districts never recovered.

Cork took three for 18 from nine impressive overs, Darren Gough was on a hat-trick at one point and finished with three for 23 in 5.4 overs, while all-rounder Craig White's form continued with three for 17 in seven overs.
After Atherton's dismissal, opener Nick Knight and Alec Stewart put on 77 in 131 balls before both were out within six deliveries for 39 and 40 respectively.
